blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why the first bottle of soda quenches your thirst more than the second or third? This is an example of consumer behaviour in action.

blocks.markdown: In economics, understanding how consumers make choices is crucial. This involves concepts like utility, marginal utility, and consumer equilibrium, which help explain how consumers maximize their satisfaction with limited resources.

blocks.title: Total Utility and Marginal Utility
blocks.text: Total utility is the total satisfaction a consumer derives from consuming a certain quantity of goods or services. Marginal utility is the additional satisfaction gained from consuming one more unit of a good or service.

blocks.markdown: The law of diminishing marginal utility states that as a consumer consumes more units of a good, the additional satisfaction from each additional unit decreases. This principle helps explain why consumers are willing to pay less for additional units.

blocks.title: Calculating Marginal Utility
blocks.prompt: Aisha consumes apples. The total utility from consuming 1 apple is 10 utils, and from 2 apples is 18 utils. What is the marginal utility of the second apple?

steps.text: Identify the total utility from consuming 1 apple: 10 utils.
Identify the total utility from consuming 2 apples: 18 utils.
Calculate the marginal utility of the second apple: \( 18 - 10 = 8 \) utils.

blocks.answer: The marginal utility of the second apple is 8 utils.

blocks.markdown: Consumer equilibrium occurs when a consumer allocates their income in such a way that the last naira spent on each good provides the same level of marginal utility. This is where consumers maximize their total utility given their budget constraint.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: When answering questions on consumer equilibrium, remember to mention both the budget constraint and the equalization of marginal utility per naira spent.

points: Total utility is the overall satisfaction from consuming goods, while marginal utility is the satisfaction from the last unit consumed.
The law of diminishing marginal utility explains why additional units of a good provide less satisfaction.
Consumer equilibrium is achieved when the marginal utility per naira is equal across all goods.
